plan.approach: Career changer: connect bakery experience to web work and assess practical project skills.

questions.question: What problem did your bakery stock tracker web app solve and what was your role in building it?
questions.why: The job asks for a first project; this checks Lukas’s concrete project experience and contributions.
rubric: Describes the specific problem the app addressed
States their personal role and main tasks
Mentions at least one outcome or improvement from the app

questions.topic: building a small feature with Flask/HTML/CSS
questions.question: Describe how you would add a form to update a shop's opening hours using HTML/CSS and a small Flask backend endpoint.
questions.why: Role requires building pages/forms and small Flask backend work; this checks practical understanding of end-to-end implementation.
rubric: Explains the front-end form structure and validation
Mentions the backend endpoint and how data is handled
Notes at least one consideration for persisting or validating data

questions.topic: working with customers and fixing bugs
questions.question: Tell me about a time you handled feedback from a bakery customer or staff and how you translated it into a change or fix.
questions.why: HeadBook values customer-facing empathy and bug-fix follow-through; Lukas’s baking role likely involved feedback and iterative changes.
rubric: Gives a specific example involving feedback
Explains the change or fix they implemented
Describes the result or how they verified the change worked

exchanges.interviewer: Hello, thank you for joining HeadBook for the Junior Web Developer interview. To start, what problem did your bakery stock tracker web app solve and what was your role in building it?
exchanges.candidate: We never knew how much flour and butter we had, so we over-ordered. I built the whole app myself: a Flask backend with SQLite, an HTML form for the morning counts, deployed on a Raspberry Pi in the back office. Flour waste went down by about 18 percent in three months.

exchanges.interviewer:
That's a clear, measurable impact—well done.  

Describe how you would add a form to update a shop's opening hours using HTML/CSS and a small Flask backend endpoint.
exchanges.candidate: Honestly, I've never written any Flask or HTML myself. A friend built the whole tracker for us, I only used it at the bakery, so I'd have to ask him how to do that.

exchanges.interviewer: I understand. Earlier you said you built the whole app yourself, but now you say you didn't write Flask or HTML. Can you clarify which parts you actually implemented versus what your friend did?
exchanges.candidate: My friend did all of it. I just typed in the counts every morning and told him when something looked wrong.

exchanges.interviewer:
Thanks for clarifying that.  

Tell me about a time you handled feedback from a bakery customer or staff and how you translated it into a change or fix.
exchanges.candidate: The morning bakers said typing numbers on the small screen was annoying, so we replaced the text fields with plus and minus buttons. After that the counts were entered in half the time and there were fewer typos.

exchanges.interviewer: Noted. Earlier you said you only entered counts and didn't build the app, but now you're describing implementing plus/minus buttons—did you suggest that change to your friend or were you the one who implemented it?
exchanges.candidate: I suggested it after the bakers complained, and my friend implemented it. I tested it the next morning with the bakers.

evaluations.asked: What problem did your bakery stock tracker web app solve and what was your role in building it?

criteria.criterion: Describes the specific problem the app addressed
States their personal role and main tasks
Mentions at least one outcome or improvement from the app
Answers clearly and to the point
Gives concrete specifics, such as an example, a detail, a number or a name, instead of only general statements

evaluations.feedback: You clearly described the problem (over-ordering because stock wasn't tracked) and a concrete result—"Flour waste went down by about 18 percent in three months"—which worked well. To improve, say explicitly how you measured that 18% (what baseline and how you tracked waste) so the interviewer can trust the result.

evaluations.topic: building a small feature with Flask/HTML/CSS
evaluations.asked: Describe how you would add a form to update a shop's opening hours using HTML/CSS and a small Flask backend endpoint.

criteria.criterion: Explains the front-end form structure and validation
Mentions the backend endpoint and how data is handled
Notes at least one consideration for persisting or validating data
What the candidate says is technically correct
Gives concrete specifics, such as an example, a detail, a number or a name, instead of only general statements
Stays consistent with what they said to earlier questions

evaluations.feedback: The interviewer asked you to describe adding a form and backend endpoint, but your answer said you haven't written Flask or HTML and so didn't explain the front-end structure, endpoint, or persistence. Next time, if you haven't implemented it, say that up front and then describe step-by-step how you would do it (for example, the form fields, client-side validation, a POST /hours endpoint, and saving to the existing datastore).

evaluations.topic: working with customers and fixing bugs
evaluations.asked: Tell me about a time you handled feedback from a bakery customer or staff and how you translated it into a change or fix.

criteria.criterion: Gives a specific example involving feedback
Explains the change or fix they implemented
Describes the result or how they verified the change worked
Describes a real situation, the candidate's task or goal in it, what they did themselves and the result (STAR: situation, task, action, result)
Gives concrete specifics, such as an example, a detail, a number or a name, instead of only general statements

evaluations.feedback: It worked that you gave a concrete change—"replaced the text fields with plus and minus buttons"—and that you tested it with the bakers. To make this stronger, when you describe the result, add the measurement method (how you timed the entries or counted typos) so the interviewer can judge the impact.
